A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATLAS research. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all 23 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: V2 reports original ATLAS evaluations against static baselines, psychometric and ranking analyses, and experiments across 57 MMLU subjects in Appendix G.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds ranking-stability, distribution-shift, local-dependence and estimator-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The proposed ATLAS pipeline and Algorithm 1 retain 3PL calibration, common-person linking, top-five randomesque selection, EAP updates and precision-based stopping. The new 2PL and alternative-reference experiments test sensitivity without revising the default method.

E1.justification: The five main benchmarks and all 57 MMLU subjects are retained. Section 4.6 adds ARC generalization scenarios targeting a completely withheld Mixtral family and later-release models, extending evaluation beyond the original random-split setting.

E2.justification: V3 newly evaluates a 2PL alternative against default 3PL ATLAS in Table 12. The original comparator membership—Random100, TinyBenchmarks, MetaBench-Primary and MetaBench-Secondary—remains unchanged; Table 13 varies the reference estimator rather than adding an external baseline.

E3.justification: V3 adds disjoint split-half ranking comparisons, related-benchmark consistency tests, ARC family and temporal holdouts, Q3 diagnostics, and parameterization/reference-estimator controls. Section 4.6 specifies calibration/test cohorts of 3,296/321 and 2,998/322 models. These substantially expand evaluation design while retaining the original main settings.

E4.justification: New analyses test ranking reproducibility and cross-benchmark consistency (Section 4.5), family and temporal robustness (Section 4.6), local independence (Appendix C.3), and sensitivity to 3PL versus 2PL and WLE versus EAP references (Appendices G.3–G.4). These address several previously untested validity questions.

E5.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 4 newly report averaging split-half correlations over ten random partitions. This concerns a new analysis, not increased repetitions of the original experiments. Existing MAE standard errors across models remain unchanged, without added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All original table values, including the complete MMLU results, are retained. Five new tables report stability, transfer, Q3 and sensitivity findings: Table 4 reports WinoGrande correlations of 0.943 for raw-accuracy rankings versus 0.981 for ability rankings; Table 5 adds temporal ARC ability MAE of 0.126 at the 0.1 stopping threshold. These are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The IRT, Fisher-information and EAP equations, calibration-complexity argument, metric definitions and p-IRT derivation are retained. Revised parameter explanations clarify the existing 3PL formula; the new diagnostics and sensitivity tests do not introduce formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly adds greater ranking stability across subsets and related domains, and makes transfer to unseen families and newer model populations a principal contribution. This expands the claimed validation scope, although the abstract, conclusion and headline efficiency claims remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds targeted qualifications: the lower asymptote may reflect priors, prompting, decoding, memorization or heuristics rather than literal guessing, and 3PL is not universally superior to 2PL. Appendix C.3 also interprets sparse residual dependence as potentially arising from shared templates or topics.

D1.justification: V3 documents construction details for the new transfer cohorts, including Mixtral exclusion, the 2024-05-01 release cutoff and exclusion of 844 models lacking release dates. Existing calibration and implementation disclosures remain, and removing '.git' from the repository URL does not establish changed resource access.

R1.justification: V3 adds Habba et al. (2026), Rodriguez et al. (2021), and Q3-related sources by Yen, Christensen and colleagues, and Marais; it removes Zhuang et al. (2023). Positioning relative to TinyBenchmarks, MetaBench and Fluid Benchmarking remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the contribution paragraph and parameter explanations, condenses part of the discussion, swaps the two existing item-informativeness/performance-extremes subsections, and adds analysis subsections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Displays are resized and relocated, Figures 2 and 3 exchange numbering and order, and five new tables are added. Existing appendix tables and figures are retained and reflowed.

improvement.justification: V2 inferred better measurement largely from reconstruction accuracy, rank reordering and examples. V3 directly tests ranking stability and transfer (Tables 4–5), checks local independence (Table 8), and examines parameterization and reference-estimator sensitivity (Tables 12–13). These address central validation gaps and add useful qualifications about 3PL, substantially strengthening the paper. Transfer evidence remains limited to ARC and one held-out family.
